# AQ host catalog 2.3.0

Epic 0, delivery by playbook (spec 0016 section 6). This bundle lets a
playbook decide what happens to a task's result: publish it to the forge, open
a pull request, wait for its checks, merge it and complete the task, or send
the task back to its agent, or hold it. Code provides the operations, the facts
and the event; the playbook decides.

It is compiled in only with the cargo feature `delivery_playbook`
(`aq_playbooks_cli::catalog::catalog_v2_3`).

## What it adds to 2.2.0

One event:
- `aq.work.result_ready` `{task_id, project_id, attempt_id, result_id,
  version}`: a task has a result that nothing has settled. It is sent by the
  host, level-triggered like `aq.work.route_needed` (no correlation fields),
  so a run that ends without settling the result is followed by another.

Ten commands. The first four answer at once (10 s); the others are
asynchronous: they answer `accepted {handle}`, then one completion on
`aq.delivery.completed`, which a playbook reads with a join (60 s to admit).
All are mutations, replayed only with their idempotency key.

| Command | Input | Outcomes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `work.complete` | `task`, `result_id` | `completed`, `refused` |
| `work.return` | `task`, `result_id`, `reason` (a code), `detail?`, `update_from_main` | `returned`, `refused` |
| `work.hold` | `task`, `result_id`, `reason` (a code) | `held` |
| `supervisor.notify` | `project`, `identity`, `text` | `sent`, `duplicate` |
| `main.sync` | `project` | `synced {head}`, `refused` |
| `branch.publish` | `task` | `published {head}`, `conflict`, `refused` |
| `pull_request.open` | `task` | `opened {number, url}`, `refused` |
| `pull_request.await_checks` | `task`, `required?`, `deadline_ms` | `passed`, `failed {names}`, `conflict`, `closed`, `timeout` |
| `pull_request.merge` | `task`, `method` (`merge`, `squash`, `rebase`), `expected_head_sha` | `merged`, `conflict`, `not_mergeable`, `refused` |
| `pull_request.close` | `task` | `closed` |

`pull_request.merge` also deletes the task's branch on the forge and in the
central git. `pull_request.await_checks` sends exactly one final completion.

One completion event, which the commands above need because the model
requires each asynchronous command to name a registered completion event:
- `aq.delivery.completed` `{outcome, output}`: the answer to
  `main.sync`, `branch.publish`, `pull_request.open`,
  `pull_request.await_checks`, `pull_request.merge` and `pull_request.close`.
  Join the handle; do not start a playbook on it. It has no subject or
  revision.

One changed command:
- `work.read` 2.3.0 (the 2.1.0 `candidate.prepare` precedent: the version
  becomes the catalog's, the capability stays `work.read`). The facts of
  2.2.0 are unchanged; eight facts of the task's latest result are added, all
  always present: `outcome`, `changed`, `branch`, `head`, `base`, `main_head`,
  `returns` and `pull_request` (`null`, or `{number, url, state, mergeable,
  checks: {state, failed}}`). A 2.2.0 answer no longer fits the 2.3.0
  contract, so an artifact sealed on 2.2.0 pins `work.read` 1.0.0, not this
  one; every other 2.2.0 contract is byte-identical.

Reasons are codes, never sentences: `checks_failed`, `checks_timed_out`,
`merge_conflict`, `not_mergeable`, `policy`, `publish_conflict`,
`pull_request_closed`, `returns_exhausted`. `detail` and `text` are fact values
or the document's own sentence.

## Files

- `registry.json`: the serialized `aq_playbooks_model::Registry`, generated by
  `write_catalog_v2_3` in
  `crates/aq-playbooks-cli/tests/catalog_v2_3_contract.rs` (run with
  `--features delivery_playbook -- --ignored`). A test checks that the
  committed bytes are what the generator writes.
- `manifest.json`: the version, fingerprint and vocabularies, `supersedes`
  (2.2.0), `commands_added`, `commands_changed` and `events_added`.
- `fixtures.json`: the valid and invalid `cases` (those of 2.2.0, with the
  result facts added to its `work.read` facts, plus the new contracts) and the
  `compatibility` section: the 2.2.0 base, the unchanged and added
  fingerprints, and `work.read` as the one changed command.
- `notes.json`: for every command and event, what an authoring agent needs
  beyond the schema. It is rendered into `CATALOG.md`
  (`aq_playbooks_compiler::docs::catalog_2_3`).
- `examples/deliver-by-playbook/`: an example source (`source.md`,
  `draft.json`, `record.json`, `facts.json`, `catalog.json`). On
  `aq.work.result_ready` it publishes the branch, opens a pull request, waits
  for checks, merges and completes; on `failed` it returns the task while
  `returns` is below `definitions.max_returns` (`lt` on the fact), otherwise
  holds it and notifies the supervisor. The contract test checks and seals it.

Fingerprint: see `manifest.json`; it is `aq_playbooks_model::digest(&("2.3.0",
&registry))`.
